title: CallLint Safe-install Presentation Content
description: The structured presentation-content document (calllint.presentation-content.v1) that makes Safe-install wording, above-the-fold ordering, and visual tokens CONFIGURABLE without letting configuration reach the decision plane (new15 Workstream P; ADR 0058). Every section here is L0/L1/L2 by ADR 0058 §1's mechanical test: its values cannot reach `contractDigest`. L3 behavioral semantics — the four verdict labels, the reason-code set, `installability`, `recommendedNextAction` and its `kind`, and AGENT_GUIDANCE's protocol steps/mustAsk/mustStop/prohibitedShortcuts — are STRUCTURALLY absent: this schema is closed at every level (`additionalProperties: false`) and no property name anywhere is drawn from the reserved L3 vocabulary, so there is no shape a document can take that carries one. Configuration SELECTS among orderings and vocabularies the code already implements; it never invents (§3). PR P-1 ships this schema, its validator, and the digest seams; PR P-2 populates `apps/web/content/**` against it and must reproduce the served tree byte for byte (§4).

schema.description: Wire identity (ADR 0043/0055 §5). The tag, not the filename, is the contract.

locale.description: BCP-47 tag this document supplies copy for. One document per locale; the emit edge selects.

authorityCopy.description: L2 security-explanation copy; security-owner review. Destination: apps/web/content/safe-install/authority-copy/<locale>.json

sectionTitles.description: L1 copy for the renderer's FIXED section keys. A key is a shipped section; config cannot add one.

guardConversion.description: L1 continuous-protection offer copy. Never an authorization: the offer's effect is code (ADR 0058 §6).

agentRelayCopy.description: L1 relay wording an agent may echo to a human (new15 §20.2). NEVER AgentProtocolPolicy (§20.1) — protocol steps and triggers stay code (ADR 0058 §6).

layout.description: L1 selection among orderings the renderer already supports (ADR 0058 §3).

tokens.description: L0 visual tokens. Referencing a stylesheet from the page is PR P-4b only — the single Workstream P PR permitted to change served bytes (ADR 0058 §4).

overrides.description: The five permitted per-resource structured overrides (ADR 0058 §3). Per-resource HTML/CSS/JS/agent-instructions are forbidden.

copyText.description: One human-facing string. Bounded so a config edit cannot smuggle a document into a page.

installability.description: The five shipped human/route states. Keys only — the ROUTE is derived from the verdict in code and is not configurable.

authority.description: The ten shipped adoption authorities (ADOPTION_AUTHORITIES). Config supplies WORDING per shipped token; it may not add, rename, or coin one (ADR 0058 §3).

displayGroup.description: The six shipped above-the-fold display groups (new14 §7). A closed set: config may reorder, never add or delete (ADR 0058 §3).

decisionCopy.description: Per-state cognitive copy. The four verdict keys and five installability keys are the shipped vocabularies; a document supplies wording for them and cannot introduce a state.

states.description: Keyed by the shipped installability states.

stateCopy.description: Wording for one shipped state. `headline` is the page's L1 headline slot — it is NOT the sealed contract's publicObservation.publicLabel, which is L3 and stays code (ADR 0058 §6). The validator additionally forbids a headline or primaryAction that impersonates a DIFFERENT state's shipped default, so config can reword but never make one disposition read as another.

authorityCopy.description: L2 wording per shipped authority token, split by whether the capability was OBSERVED or was a meaningful, evidence-supported ABSENCE. Absence wording must stay an observation and is never rendered as denied/absent/impossible (ADR 0058 §3); the validator enforces that phrase set. Named `*Phrases` deliberately: `observed` alone is a RESERVED L3 key (it is DecisionAuthorityFact.observed, the boolean that records what evidence showed), and these are phrase maps keyed BY that disposition, not the fact itself.

sectionTitles.description: Titles for the renderer's fixed sections. `publisherBlock` is the quarantine label (INV-2.4-05): its wording is configurable, its POSITION is not — no config may relocate publisher text into a decision group (ADR 0058 §6).

agentRelayCopy.description: The six new15 §20.2 relay slots. Relay copy may never add or remove a protocol trigger (ADR 0058 §6); it is wording an agent echoes, not policy an agent obeys. new15 §5 names FOUR relay slots and this block declares six: the extra two (`adds`, `notObserved`) are not invented copy — each names a field the sealed contract already carries, so §5's four are the MINIMUM. The rule that keeps the superset honest is enforced rather than asserted: EVERY slot below names a contract field or a plan fact as its BASIS, and a sentence whose basis is absent is not emitted at all. A seventh slot with no basis fails that check. Each `description` records its own basis so the reconciliation lives beside the declaration.

headline.description: BASIS: publicObservation.verdict + publicLabel. Unconditional — a resolved contract always carries a verdict.

reason.description: BASIS: publicObservation.reasonCodes + evidenceLevel. Reason codes are NAMED from the contract, never paraphrased into new claims.

adds.description: BASIS: authorityDelta.adds. Emitted only when that array is non-empty — an "adds" sentence with nothing to add would be decoration, not a projection. (Measured: non-empty on 17 of 19 served identities.)

notObserved.description: BASIS: authorityDelta.notObserved, gated on publicObservation.completeness === "complete" exactly as the contract builder gates it. When the inventory is partial, silence is a GAP rather than evidence of absence, so the sentence must not appear — absence of evidence is recorded as absence, never as safety.

approvalQuestion.description: BASIS: a computed planDigest. Without one there is no exact plan to approve, so the question would invite approval of something unnamed.

guardOffer.description: BASIS: the guard tool's own typed outcome fields (enabled: false, requiresSeparateAuthorization: true). Configurable WORDING, not configurable MEANING — a configured string can restate the fact differently but cannot make it untrue, and cannot cause the tool to install anything.

groupOrder.description: A PERMUTATION of the six shipped groups: exactly six entries, all distinct. Enforcing the full set is what makes this a selection rather than an invention — a document cannot drop `consequence` to hide it, nor add a seventh group the renderer has no slot for (ADR 0058 §3).

maxAuthorityFacts.description: Upper bound on rendered authority facts. Capped at the shipped 5 — config may show fewer, never more (ADR 0059).

maxSecondaryLinks.description: Upper bound on secondary links. Capped at the shipped 2.

tokensVersion.description: Machine token identifying the deployed apps/web/styles/** set. Deliberately not prose.

stylesheetHref.description: Site-absolute path only — no scheme, no host, so a config edit can never point a page at a third-party origin. A page only REFERENCES this from PR P-4b onward (ADR 0058 §4).

resources.description: Keyed by canonical slug. Every value is limited to the five permitted fields; none may affect a decision field (ADR 0058 §3).

resourceOverride.description: The exhaustive permitted per-resource override set (ADR 0058 §3). Per-resource HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and agent instructions are forbidden and have no representation here.

originalSetupUrl.description: A known publisher setup page. https only; never rendered as a command and never followed by the engine.

expiresAt.description: When this override lapses. An expired override is inert, never an error — presentation must fail open to CODE defaults, never to a blank page.
